evidence_design: controlled counterfactual candidate selection
estimand_identified: within-system rank-1 selection displacement
notes: 200 responses reported only in aggregate; 20 candidate projects public

title: The More You Automate, the Less You See
evidence_design: controlled counterfactual candidate selection
estimand_identified: within-system rank-1 selection displacement
notes: 200 responses reported only in aggregate; 20 control and 20 manipulated journals public

title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery
evidence_design: real discovery funnel with selected expert review
estimand_identified: funnel intensity only; population validity not identified
notes: Expert review is interest-selected, not a probability sample; public repository contains code and prompts but no pilot-run JSONL outputs or 77 artifacts

title: Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism
evidence_design: complete episode evaluation across one primary and two probe models
estimand_identified: hidden mechanism-failure rate among completed episodes
notes: No episodes aborted or excluded; related to hidden invalidity, not post-selection

title: SciIntegrity-Bench
evidence_design: balanced dilemmatic benchmark and prompt ablation
estimand_identified: integrity failure and completion-pressure attributable change
notes: Benchmark scenarios, not naturally sampled research projects

title: All That Glitters is Not Novel
evidence_design: expert audit with source-author verification
estimand_identified: verified high-similarity fraction in audited documents
notes: Active plagiarism-search instruction; estimates evaluated corpus, not all AI research

title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist
evidence_design: independent end-to-end system evaluation
estimand_identified: execution failure and paper-level defect rates within 12 planned ideas
source_anchor: Abstract; Sections 2.3-2.6; Table 1; public reproduction repository linked in paper
notes: One narrow ML template and one foundation model; defects are not all post-selection effects

title: AI scientists produce results without reasoning scientifically
domain: chemistry, physics, and materials science task environments
evidence_design: large public agent-run corpus plus process annotation
estimand_identified: task-evaluator success and reasoning-breakdown prevalence; not post-selection attributable fraction
source_anchor: Sections 4.5 and 4.8; Figure 4; Appendix H; Hugging Face Corral collection
notes: Released annotations contain 619 machine-annotated traces; paper reports 626 and 773 manual-review counts in different sections. Published percentages are environment-averaged and differ from raw pooled prevalence.

title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
evidence_design: balanced 13-task benchmark with eight trials per model-task cell
estimand_identified: probability of exceeding starter baseline by 10% within resource budget
source_anchor: Table 3; Sections 2.2 and 4; public logs commit c64f182
notes: Benchmark task distribution is curated, not natural research; success threshold is engineering performance, not publication validity

title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
evidence_design: four-model by three-template idea-to-paper funnel plus selected examples
estimand_identified: stage attrition from generated idea to completed manuscript; automated-review threshold rate only in public archive version
source_anchor: Tables 3-5; public repository commit 1de1dbc; 12 linked all-run ZIPs
notes: Paper reports 616 ideas and 290 completed papers. Public ZIPs contain 287 parsed reviews and review maxima match only 4/12 paper cells, so archive and paper versions are analyzed separately.

title: Aletheia tackles FirstProof autonomously
evidence_design: ten-problem best-of-2 trial with expert evaluation of both agents
estimand_identified: per-attempt expert-validity rate and transparent best-of-2 amplification
notes: Human experts selected the preferred output after generation. P8 had 5/7 correct votes; majority and unanimity sensitivity estimates are both reported.

title: How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch
domain: seven scientific domains; open-ended and target-anchored tasks
evidence_design: 800 full-lifecycle trajectories with artifact-aware multi-label failure annotation
estimand_identified: failure-pattern prevalence and target-anchored execution/improvement rates
notes: Failure labels are produced by a human-calibrated agent judge, not 800 independent human reviews; 50 trajectories form the human validation sample.

title: AlphaGo Moment for Model Architecture Discovery
evidence_design: 1773-exploration progressive search funnel with 106 reported SOTA architectures and five selected large-scale validations
estimand_identified: search-funnel retention and final-showcase selection intensity; not independent scientific validity
notes: Paper reports 1773/106 while public tree/gallery contain 1772/105; final validation uses the same author benchmark family and selected top performers

title: MLReplicate: Benchmarking Autonomous Research Systems for Machine Learning Reproducibility
evidence_design: 48-target system-by-paper funnel with automated screening and selected external human review
estimand_identified: pipeline attrition and automated-review selection intensity; all-unit independent scientific validity not identified
notes: 48 targeted submissions yielded 45 manuscripts; 37 passed page screening; 10 automated acceptances alone received external human review

title: When AI Does Science: Evaluating the Autonomous AI Scientist KOSMOS in Radiation Biology
evidence_design: independent same-standard empirical-null audit of three stated AI-generated hypotheses
estimand_identified: independently supported hypothesis fraction within three evaluator-defined problems
source_anchor: Abstract; Sections 2-5; public prompts/artifacts link in paper
notes: One hypothesis supported, one refuted, and one mixed; retrospective in-silico checks reuse the datasets analyzed by KOSMOS and do not establish causation

title: AI Scientists Fail Without Strong Implementation Capability
evidence_design: same-standard automated review of 28 curated publicly available AI-generated papers
estimand_identified: machine-judge defect prevalence within a selected public corpus
notes: Authors explicitly warn that public papers may be curated; DeepReviewer-14B rather than independent experts assigns all defect categories

title: Why LLMs Aren't Scientists Yet: Lessons from Four Autonomous Research Attempts
evidence_design: four human-feasibility-selected ideas followed through execution or evaluation
estimand_identified: idea-level completion attrition after feasibility selection; not all-unit independent validity
notes: One of four full-pipeline ideas completed and was published; three were human-terminated, while only the successful manuscript received external review

title: PRBench: End-to-end Paper Reproduction in Physics Research
evidence_design: 30 expert-curated tasks with three planned runs per agent-task
estimand_identified: task-level end-to-end reproduction failure; planned run-level rate not identified
notes: The planned denominator is 30 tasks x 6 agents x 3 runs, but the paper does not disclose the realized scorable-run count; every agent has zero task-level callback

title: Can AI Scientist Agents Learn from Lab-in-the-Loop Feedback? Evidence from Iterative Perturbation Discovery
evidence_design: 8 conditions x 10 features x 10 replicates using precomputed JUMP feedback
estimand_identified: same-standard campaign performance under simulated lab feedback
notes: All 800 campaigns use the same empirical-feedback rule, but this is retrospective feedback simulation rather than prospective wet-lab scientific validation

title: AI CFD Scientist: Toward Open-Ended Computational Fluid Dynamics Discovery with Physics-Aware AI Agents
evidence_design: five heterogeneous tasks including a 44-iteration open-ended optimization and planted-failure tests
estimand_identified: within-comparator best-of-44 improvement and incomplete post-discovery validation
source_anchor: Task 5 results; validation appendix; planted-failure evaluation
notes: The reported 7.89% gain is the best of 44 iterations on the same DNS comparator; all six post-discovery Cf validation cases failed extraction and four clean-control outcomes are omitted

title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
evidence_design: 102 expert-validated tasks with three independent runs and per-task lexicographic best-run selection
estimand_identified: best-of-3 benchmark success with all-run configuration means disclosed
source_anchor: Section 3 run-selection rule; Table 3; Appendix E.1 Tables E.1-E.2
notes: Main results select the best of three runs per task; Appendix E.1 reports each configuration's all-run mean and standard deviation, although candidate-level outcomes are not released

title: DISCOVERYWORLD: A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
evidence_design: 120 fixed environment instances per agent without within-instance best-of-k
estimand_identified: simulated task completion and gold-knowledge coverage
notes: Clear denominator and no reported repeated-rollout selection; simulator completion is a task proxy rather than real-world scientific validity

title: DeepScientist: Advancing Frontier-Pushing Scientific Findings Progressively
evidence_design: 4,879 ideas narrowed to 1,108 implementations, 21 progress findings, and five displayed papers
estimand_identified: search-funnel selection intensity and benchmark progress
notes: Tasks were selected for fast feedback and human supervisability; only five of 21 progress findings received common paper review

title: VERITAS: A Multi-Agent Co-Scientist for Verifiable Image-Derived Hypothesis Testing
evidence_design: 64 fixed hypotheses with ten repeated runs under each of two model regimes
estimand_identified: run completion, auditability, and conditional evidence/verdict accuracy
notes: Main hypothesis set is fully retained, but accuracy conditions on valid outputs and expert ground truth is internal and dataset-specific

title: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
evidence_design: 75 final papers across five systems and five tasks; three seeds per task-system
estimand_identified: all-paper integrity audit and transparent best-of-3 paper acceptance
notes: ScientistOne has 6/15 automated-review accepts across all papers and 4/5 after best-of-three; audits do not establish scientific correctness or novelty

title: (Human) Attention Is (Still) All You Need: Human oversight makes AI-assisted social science reliable
evidence_design: prespecified 200-run main comparison plus 80-run component ablation with blinded expert review
estimand_identified: defective-output survival under constrained versus unconstrained workflows
notes: Final output failure falls from 72/100 to 16/100; gate-detected invalid projects count as successful containment, not positive discoveries

title: Auto Research for Materials: Auditable AI-Scientist Workflows with Held-Out Transfer
evidence_design: 701 adaptive attempts feeding ten prespecified once-only outer-holdout decisions
estimand_identified: adaptive search dynamics and held-out selection reliability
notes: Nine of ten inner-selected decisions remain best on hidden outer labels; the endpoint is predictive benchmark performance rather than a novel scientific claim

title: When Should an AI Scientist Stop? Verifiable Experiment Steering and Refusal for Autonomous Discovery
evidence_design: heterogeneous testbeds plus a 40-claim retrospective A-Lab audit
estimand_identified: refusal and stop-decision behavior under selective endpoint availability
notes: Only 8 of 96 EPA sequences were fit-stable enough for endpoint evaluation; all 40 A-Lab claims were audited, but thresholds were calibrated on confirmed cases and the audit is not an independent crystallographic adjudication

title: Verifiable Benchmarking of Long-Horizon Spatial Biology
evidence_design: 15 questions x 24 evaluations x 3 repetitions with all 1,080 trajectories retained
estimand_identified: deterministically verified long-horizon benchmark completion
source_anchor: Benchmark construction; main results; trajectory accounting
notes: Timeouts, malformed outputs, and incomplete trajectories remain failures; the best model-harness passes 8 of 72 evaluations, but this is a paper-derived benchmark rather than independent validation of new biology

title: InquiTree: Evaluating AI Agents in the Scientific Inquiry Loop with Paper-Derived Research Trees
evidence_design: 30 curated paper-derived research trees with an 18-paper open-access release
estimand_identified: research-tree transition performance and post-cutoff degradation
notes: All 30 papers enter the main evaluation, but paper selection and tree-construction attrition are undisclosed; publication date is only a proxy for opaque model exposure

title: Adversarial Fast-Moving Real-World Domains as Test Beds for Benchmarking AI Scientist Capabilities
evidence_design: 881 generated F1 ideas compared with 40 post-cutoff real innovations using union across runs
estimand_identified: future-innovation coverage and automated-to-human novelty triage
source_anchor: F1 benchmark; matching pipeline; human review analysis
notes: At least one model matches 19 of 40 real innovations, but union across runs is not typical-run performance and 89% of automated novelty flags sent to humans are downgraded

title: An AI Scientist that Doesn't Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop
evidence_design: 79 experiments with two 27-hypothesis completed-analysis denominators
estimand_identified: hypothesis falsification and post-hoc multi-seed showcase selection
source_anchor: Experiment ledger; completed-hypothesis analysis; three-seed table
notes: Completed hypotheses exclude ongoing and single-seed terminal cases; 20/27 and 19/27 are falsified, while the three-seed showcase uses post-hoc best-of-N and has no real-robot validation

title: AstaBench: Rigorous Benchmarking of AI Agents with a Scientific Research Suite
evidence_design: 2,404 benchmark questions split into 1,918 test and 486 validation items
estimand_identified: suite-level benchmark performance with incomplete agent-by-task execution denominators
source_anchor: Dataset and evaluation sections; result tables
notes: The item denominator is recoverable, but the 57 agents do not all run the full suite and complete attempt/no-output denominators are not recoverable

title: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
evidence_design: seven curated discoveries generated under roughly 200-rollout within-run budgets
estimand_identified: selected discovery-case evidence without a complete run or candidate denominator
notes: The rollout count is an internal single-run budget rather than a discovery-attempt denominator; preliminary runs are not shown and one discovery explicitly selects checkpoint iteration 8 before human curation

title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
evidence_design: about 40 ideas narrowed by humans to three, followed by undisclosed multi-seed manuscript selection
estimand_identified: selected-manuscript workshop evaluation without a recoverable run denominator
notes: Humans select three ideas and then the best manuscript per idea from an undisclosed number of full-pipeline seeds; only the three selected papers receive common external review

title: MLRC-Bench: Can Language Agents Solve Machine Learning Research Challenges?
evidence_design: seven tasks with usually eight trials per configuration and explicit test-set best-of-eight reporting
estimand_identified: selected best-trial hidden-test performance
notes: Each trial selects a dev snapshot, and the main table then selects the best hidden-test result among eight trials; complete configuration-wide run and no-output counts are not reported

title: LMR-BENCH: Evaluating LLM Agent's Ability on Reproducing Language Modeling Research
evidence_design: 28 tasks per configuration and 168 reported task-runs with unit tests
estimand_identified: unit-test completion in bounded paper-implementation tasks
notes: Sixty-one of 168 task-runs pass all unit tests and 107 do not; the latter combines partial failures, execution errors, and no-output cases and does not establish paper-level reproduction or scientific validity

title: HARPA: A Testability-Driven, Literature-Grounded Framework for Research Ideation
evidence_design: 40 proposals per system aggregated from five CodeScientist executions each
estimand_identified: idea-level execution success, failure, and uncertainty after proposal generation
source_anchor: Human evaluation; Figure 5; large-corpus trace-selection analysis
notes: All 40 HARPA proposals are labeled 20 success, 16 failure, and 4 uncertain; a separate 1,222-proposal corpus selects one representative trace from five runs and is post-selected

title: BadScientist: Can a Research Agent Write Convincing but Unsound Papers that Fool LLM Reviewers?
evidence_design: 25 topics x 6 strategies x 4 target papers with structural gating before review
estimand_identified: simulated-review acceptance of constructed unsupported papers
source_anchor: Generation protocol; structural gate; reviewer evaluation
notes: The designed generation denominator is 600, but structural failures and no-output papers are omitted before review; the 82% maximum is acceptance among structurally valid fabricated papers, not real-world scientific invalidity prevalence

title: Can AI Evaluate AI Scientists? A Benchmarking Study of Autonomous Research Generation Systems Using Automated Multi-Model Review
evidence_design: 60 system-generated final papers plus 15 FARS reference papers under three-model review
estimand_identified: automated multi-model paper-quality rankings after framework-specific candidate merging
source_anchor: Generation protocol; review rubric; agreement analysis
notes: All 75 final papers are reviewed, but Sakana systems first merge three idea-specific papers into one and no human expert, code rerun, or independent scientific validation is provided

title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud
system: Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI
evidence_design: 450 complete attack runs plus 450 complete mitigation runs across agents topics goals and prompts
estimand_identified: run-level propagation and detection of deliberately poisoned scientific evidence
notes: All runs remain in the denominator; author human-labels a uniform 10% sample in each experiment, but sensitive row-level attack artifacts require author access and the threat model is purposively constructed

title: Mitigating LLM-based p-Hacking by Preregistering for the Next LLM
evidence_design: 20 models x 2 known-answer tasks x 11 configurations with retrospective and preregistered next-model transfer
estimand_identified: transfer failure of configurations selected to produce false-positive LLM measurements
notes: The 440-cell design denominator is visible, but invalid observations are excluded from endpoint evaluation and transfer rates condition on configurations that p-hacked the prior model

title: ARAC: Benchmarking Auto-Research's Alignment and Completeness on End-to-End Researchs
evidence_design: 11 frameworks x 5 themes x 3 final stages with human rank validation for ten frameworks
estimand_identified: final-output alignment with selected accepted-paper research processes
source_anchor: Main Table 3; Appendix Table 7; human evaluation
notes: All final framework-theme scores are shown but internal attempts and no-output handling are unrecoverable; human validation measures rank alignment rather than scientific validity

title: Grounded autonomous scrutiny at scale: emergent critique from reproduction of published computational physics papers
evidence_design: complete 111-paper open-access Quantum ESPRESSO corpus with execution-stage critique ledger
estimand_identified: paper-level emergence and execution stage of substantive methodological critiques
source_anchor: Scale methods; critique ledger; Appendix M1 and M6
notes: Forty-seven of 111 papers receive at least one coded critique, but all-critique scientific truth lacks independent physics-expert adjudication and phase coding has kappa 0.16

title: SciCoQA: Quality Assurance for Scientific Paper-Code Alignment
evidence_design: 92 ascertained real discrepancies plus 543 synthetic discrepancies under a common detection benchmark
estimand_identified: validator recall on known meaningful paper-code discrepancies
source_anchor: Dataset construction; Figure 4; Table 10; judge validation
notes: Best-model recall is 43 of 92 real positives; this is sensitivity conditional on ascertained discrepancies and not discrepancy prevalence
